correctness.rationale: For independent uniform x,y on G the four random arguments x+y, x−y, x, y are pairwise independent and uniform: each pair is an invertible linear transform of (x,y), using invertibility of doubling for the sum/difference pair. For a centered function all four pullbacks in Q are therefore pairwise orthogonal in complex normalized L², with squared coefficient sum 10. The constant part maps to minus twice that constant and is orthogonal to all centered images. Thus Q*Q=10I−6Π_constants; equality in the bound is attained by the constants (listing nonzero equality cases, plus the trivial zero case). With S=G∖{0}, D sends f to −2f(0) at 0 and (P−4I)f|_S+f(0) at all other coordinates. In ordinary coordinates, equivalently after a common scalar change for the normalized measure, its block on the identity direction and the normalized S-constant direction is [−2,0;√(N−1),−3]. The squared singular values of that block have sum N+12 and product 36. The mean-zero S complement is reducing: each cycle gives permutation roots of unity, with exactly one global constant direction removed from the joint 1-eigenspace. This gives the stated multisets, including multiplicities, and λ_-≤3<9, so the least right singular space is one-dimensional inside the two-coordinate block. The eigenvector formula follows from its first Gram row. Since λ_+∼N and λ_-λ_+=36 the stated sharp asymptotics follow. When f(0) is known, subtract its contribution and use P−4I on all of S: the least singular value is exactly 3 for every group, even one-cycle groups (global S-constant eigenvector). This strengthens the frozen text's nonexclusive attainment statement and does not contradict it.
